book_title: My Dear Beloved Son or Daughter (Ayyuhal Walad)

chapters.title: Knowledge That Will Not Save You
chapters.rationale: Opens with the master's framing reply and builds the central argument that unused knowledge becomes a witness against its owner.

chapters.title: The Striving That Mercy Meets
chapters.rationale: Centers the parable of the tested worshipper and the sayings on self-reckoning, resolving the paradox between divine mercy and human striving.

chapters.title: The Hours Before Dawn
chapters.rationale: Gathers every passage on Tahajjud, the pre-dawn call, and the weeping dove into a single meditation on wakefulness and longing.

chapters.title: Worship Is Obedience, Nothing Less
chapters.rationale: Treats worship as conformity to prophetic example, with the Shibli hadith closing the case that knowledge must be measured, not heaped.

chapters.title: Eight Lessons from Thirty-Three Years
chapters.rationale: The self-contained narrative of Hatim ibn Ism's eight benefits — a complete teaching unit deserving its own chapter.

chapters.title: Finding a True Guide
chapters.rationale: Pulls together the conditions of the path, the qualities of a Shaykh al-Kamil, and the inner and outer etiquettes of discipleship.

chapters.title: Sufism, Servitude, Trust, Sincerity
chapters.rationale: Answers the disciple's four definitional questions and closes with Ghazali's counsel to stop asking and start walking.

chapters.title: Four to Avoid, Four to Embrace
chapters.rationale: The structured closing instruction — what to refuse (debate, preaching, rulers, their gifts) and what to practice (Allah, neighbor, study, restraint).

chapters.title: A Prayer for the Road
chapters.rationale: The promised du'a stands alone as the book's benediction and farewell.
